newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers steady to lower, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers steady to lower, slow trade.

text.p: North American bunker prices were steady to lower from prices earlier this week in what traders said was slow activity on tight supply.
"Markets are pretty steady but there are supply problems in Philadelphia and other ports," said one East Coast trader.
Philadelphia was heard with only one supplier who was reluctant to sell until prices crept up further.
In New York Harbor, 380 CST fell $4 to between $142 and $147 a tonne amid average demand, players said, adding they retraced $2 from Tuesday's gains. 180 CST was traded $3 lower to $147/149.
On the U.S. Gulf Coast, Houston 380 CST stayed steady, trading at $134/135 a tonne but diesel slipped $2 to $227/230. Demand was moderate.
On the West Coast, Seattle also edged down $2 to $114/116 and 180 CST dipped down $3 to $118/120 in quiet trade.
"We are all waiting to see what happens with crude oil and the Far East," said one Seattle trader. "There have been so few avails."
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
